episodes.title: “My father married my mother when she was 16. He then married her mother”
episodes.description: Jerusha has relatives who are married to Warren Jeffs , subject of the Netflix series, Keep Sweet, Pray and Obey, currently serving a life sentence in a Texan jail for sexual offences against children. Jeffs was the president of the Fundamentalist Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-Day Saints, a polygamous cult which he moved from Salt Lake City, to the Utah-Arizona border in 1998. Here is a brief extract from our interview, which you can listen to in full, above. “These men really truly see themselves as God, and women are not human, just they're just incubators and they exist to serve men. It's inherently oppressive. I think it's nearly impossible for the women and children to not be oppressed, and it's why sexual abuse with women and children is rampant.” “Our cult separated from the church and they just kind of do their own thing. And each clan make their own rules but they generally follow the Book of Mormon and some of the other religious texts and seclusion is a big part of it.” “When I go down to visit them in Hilldale [on the border of Utah and Arizona, an area notable for its history as a colony of Mormon polygamists], there's still a lot of relatives there. Three of my sisters were married when they were 16. So I feel very lucky, but I actually feel very fortunate because I had an education. And after my grandfather died, my mother's father, when I was three, my mother's mother kind of took over, but then she married my father, which they excused because they said Joseph Smith [Mormon founder] did that. He married a mother and a daughter when he took on multiple wives.” “I grew up seeing my birth father kissing my very young, beautiful mother and then turning and kissing my grandmother. And they had this belief that the end times were coming and that Jesus would return to that house specifically. And so my grandma had it in her head that we needed to all prepare.” Jerusha Vox To hear more, visit juliebindel.substack.com
